Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: May a route sketch ignore the four missing tracks?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It must record the violation and a legal redesign.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Route count across a corridor depends on legal line width, spacing, keep-outs, and layer count. Trace the visual in order: route demand; track capacity; rule check. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic corridor: 14 required traces but 10 legal tracks on one layer; change assignment, placement, or stackup and recalculate. Boundary: Track counts are synthetic teaching data.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic corridor: 14 required traces but 10 legal tracks on one layer; change assignment, placement, or stackup and recalculate. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. Track counts are synthetic teaching data.
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
